verdict.rationale: Floot's own self-hosting page says you can export both the code and the database and deploy them anywhere. Its docs also describe each project as a real TypeScript/React app whose code can be fully read or exported, and say a full SQL dump can be downloaded on any plan. The evidence is short first-party claims only, so missing for 10: step-by-step self-hosting instructions, documentation of how platform-brokered services (OAuth, email, push, scheduled jobs) behave outside Floot, and independent or hands-on confirmation that an exported app runs elsewhere.

support.subject: As a developer, I can export the full source code and run or host the app outside the platform

citations.quote: you can export the code and the database and deploy them wherever you like.
A Floot project is a real TypeScript and React app — pages, components, and backend endpoints — and you can read or export all of it.
You can download a full SQL dump of your database at any time, on any plan
